source_meta.issue links: Relates:outward:MC-279830:Fire value is not decreased for projectiles (arrows, trident) with inGround:1b
source_meta._title: Arrows and tridents on fire and stuck in the ground cannot be extinguished by rain

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 24w36a in a disposable single-player world. Use Creative mode with commands/cheats enabled as a practical execution choice. Perform the test outdoors in a biome where rain falls as rain, with an unobstructed view of the sky above both the player and the target ground. Default controls are assumed; use the equivalent bound controls if they have been changed.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher has access to the historical snapshot 24w36a.
Use a new or otherwise disposable world because the recommended version is an old snapshot.
Commands are available to the player. In single-player, create the world in Creative mode with commands/cheats enabled; on a server, the executing player would need operator permission.
Choose exposed solid ground with no roof, leaves, or other blocks above the intended arrow landing point.
Use a biome with ordinary rainfall, such as plains or forest; do not use a dry biome where rain is not visibly rendered, or a cold location where precipitation falls as snow.
Remove or move away from any pre-existing arrows before beginning so that the nearest-entity selector @n[type=minecraft:arrow] resolves to the arrow created during this test.
The plan intentionally tests the arrow reproduction described by the report. Do not substitute the trident variant, because the report does not supply an equivalent detailed trident procedure.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation using the exact Java Edition snapshot 24w36a, then launch the game with that installation.
steps.success_cue: The game reaches the title screen and identifies the running version as 24w36a.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer and create a new disposable world in Creative mode. Ensure commands or cheats are enabled before creating the world if that option is presented.
steps.success_cue: The player enters a Creative-mode world where inventory items can be rearranged freely and commands can be executed.

steps.action: Wait for initial world loading to finish before performing the reproduction.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is rendered, player movement responds normally, and opening chat does not stall while chunks load.

steps.action: Move to an outdoor location with solid exposed ground and no blocks above the intended shooting area. Use a biome where precipitation appears as rain rather than snow, and where rain is not suppressed by biome conditions.
steps.exact_input: Use the movement controls; defaults are W, A, S, D and Space.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the open, and the target ground a few blocks ahead has an unobstructed vertical path to the sky.

steps.action: Check the immediate area for existing arrows. Remove them or move far enough away that the arrow fired for this test will be the nearest arrow entity to the player.
steps.success_cue: No other arrow entity is visible near the test location, so the nearest-arrow selector can unambiguously target the test arrow.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat, enter the clear-weather command exactly as supplied in the report, and press Enter to execute it. Include the leading slash because the command is being run through in-game chat.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that the weather has been changed to clear, and no rain is falling at the test location.

steps.action: Press T, enter the supplied give command exactly, and press Enter. Do not alter the enchantment component syntax.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that a bow was given, and a bow with the Flame enchantment is present in the player's inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Press T, enter the supplied arrow give command exactly, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that an arrow was given, and at least one arrow is present in the player's inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Press E to open the inventory. Move the Flame-enchanted bow into one of the nine hotbar slots along the bottom of the inventory if it is not already there. Leave at least one arrow anywhere in the inventory. Close the inventory with E or Esc, then select the bow's hotbar slot using its number key or the mouse wheel.
steps.exact_input: E; place the Flame bow in a hotbar slot; select that slot with 1-9 or the mouse wheel.
steps.success_cue: The bow is visible in the player's hand, and at least one arrow remains available in the inventory.

steps.action: Stand approximately 2 to 5 blocks from the exposed target ground and aim the crosshair downward at the top face of a solid ground block. Keep the intended impact point directly exposed to the sky.
steps.success_cue: The crosshair points at nearby exposed ground, providing a short and deterministic path for the arrow to become embedded.

steps.action: Hold the Use Item control to draw the bow. The default input is the right mouse button. Hold it for about one second so the arrow has enough speed to reach and stick in the target block.
steps.success_cue: The bow is visibly drawn while the crosshair remains aimed at the target ground.

steps.action: Release the Use Item control to fire the arrow into the ground.
steps.success_cue: A single arrow is visibly lodged in the target ground and is visibly burning because it was fired from the Flame-enchanted bow.

steps.action: Approach the embedded arrow without touching or destroying it. Stop within a few blocks of it and keep it loaded and visible. Do not fire another arrow.
steps.success_cue: The test arrow remains embedded in the exposed ground, remains the nearest arrow entity to the player, and can be targeted by @n[type=minecraft:arrow].

steps.action: Press T, execute the supplied Fire-tag query for the first time, and press Enter. Include the leading slash.
steps.success_cue: Chat returns the Fire field for an arrow rather than reporting that no entity was found.

steps.action: Leave the arrow undisturbed and wait approximately one second before running the same query again. Do not move far enough away to unload the arrow.
steps.success_cue: The embedded arrow is still present, loaded, and remains the nearest arrow to the player after measurable game time has passed.

steps.action: Press T and execute the same Fire-tag query a second time exactly as supplied.
steps.success_cue: Chat returns a second Fire-field result for the same embedded arrow.

steps.action: Press T, execute the supplied rain command, and press Enter. Remain near the embedded arrow after issuing the command.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that the weather has been changed to rain.

steps.action: Wait until rain is visibly falling at the test location and directly reaches the exposed block containing the embedded arrow. Do not continue while the weather transition is incomplete or while chunks are unresponsive.
steps.success_cue: Visible rain is falling through the unobstructed sky at the embedded arrow, the arrow remains loaded, and normal player and chat input are responsive.

steps.action: With the player still close to the same embedded arrow, press T and execute the Fire-tag query once more.
steps.success_cue: Chat returns the post-rain Fire-field result for the embedded arrow without a target-selection error.

stor.handoff_condition: Rain is visibly falling directly onto the exposed, ground-embedded arrow, and the post-rain /data get entity @n[type=minecraft:arrow] Fire command has just returned in chat. Hand control to the observation subsystem while the arrow remains loaded and undisturbed.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, world seed, or single-player versus server requirement. This plan uses a disposable Creative-mode single-player world with commands enabled because it is the simplest deterministic way to execute the supplied commands without changing their semantics.
The report only says to stand in the open and does not name a biome. The plan uses a rain-capable biome and unobstructed sky access so that the requested rain can physically reach the projectile.

The report instructs the executor to run the first Fire query twice but does not specify a delay between those executions. The plan inserts an approximately one-second delay so that the two queries occur on distinguishable game ticks.

Although the title and expected-result text mention both arrows and tridents, the supplied reproduction commands and actions describe only an arrow. This plan therefore does not invent a separate trident procedure.
The report's exact @n selector is preserved. The plan removes other nearby arrows and keeps the player close to the test arrow to minimize ambiguity about which entity is selected.
